Criminal courts are a frequent targets of criticism from Saudi lawyers and human rights activists.

And tough bargaining continues between the justice ministry and the newly reconstituted Supreme Judicial Council because of "overlaps" in defining their new responsibilities, Mr al Gasim said.

The council says it needs its own budget and administrative control to guarantee the independence of judges, while the ministry wants to direct the judiciary's finances and administration, Mr al Gasim added.
The proposed codification, announced by Mohammed al Eissa, the Saudi justice minister in May, is likely to be another contentious undertaking.
